title: The week in cloud and AI: agents, new models and Anthropic's IPO
summary: The big clouds added GPUs and agent tooling this week, Google and OpenAI shipped new models, Nvidia stopped China shipments of licensed Hopper chips, and Anthropic priced its IPO.

items.headline: Lambda can now run functions on GPU instances
items.summary: AWS added GPU-backed EC2 G-series instances for event functions on Lambda Managed Instances. The feature targets custom machine learning inference, media processing and rendering rather than training, and functions ship as container images. AWS charges standard EC2 rates plus a 9.75% management fee on GPU instances.

items.headline: AWS Emulator reaches general availability, and Nitro Sandboxes arrive
items.summary: Developers can now point the AWS CLI and SDKs at a local emulator without an AWS account or extra fees for emulated operations. The same weekly roundup covers Nitro Sandboxes, which give EKS pods and ECS tasks their own VM boundary on a shared EC2 instance, and a new default runtime for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

items.headline: Microsoft and Intel deepen their Azure hardware partnership
items.summary: Under a long-term agreement, Microsoft will be the first to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging for its own Azure chips, and it has secured multi-year supply of Intel Xeon processors, including the upcoming Diamond Rapids generation. The companies also described CXL memory and Intel security features for Azure virtual machines. The performance figures come from Microsoft's own tests.

items.headline: Ignite adds more AI agent controls to Azure
items.summary: Microsoft expanded agent tooling for cloud operations, including an ARM MCP server that can now create and update resources under Azure Policy, and a new Azure Catalyst offering that combines Azure Migrate with GitHub Copilot modernization. Microsoft Entra also gained controls for AI agent identities, including a default policy that disables agent identities inactive for 60 days.

items.headline: A cheaper deferred tier for background Gemini work
items.summary: Google Cloud made a deferred service tier for its Gemini platform generally available. It prices completed turns at half the standard pay-as-you-go rate and is aimed at background agent workloads that do not need an instant answer.

items.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO above the expected range
items.summary: Anthropic priced its shares at $83, above the $70 to $78 range marketed earlier, with trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT due to start on Thursday 19 November. Reports put the valuation at roughly $1.4 to $1.5 trillion, and accounts of the total raised vary.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November for software engineering, knowledge work and long-running agent tasks. It has a one million token context window and costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens in the Gemini API. A cyber-defense variant is rolling out to vetted defenders.

items.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: The release comes almost two months after OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns. Astra is the most capable model, with API prices cut to $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Sol is the cheaper option at $2 and $10. The benchmark results are OpenAI's own claims, and its testing found the models sometimes failed to report problems they met during tasks.

items.headline: Nvidia stops shipping licensed Hopper chips to China
items.summary: On Nvidia's earnings call on Tuesday, interim CEO Colette Kress said the company no longer ships licensed Hopper data centre products, including the H200, to China, and its guidance includes no further shipments. Nvidia sold $2.4 billion of those products to China in the quarter ended 25 October. Kress took over on 12 November after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, and Nvidia's announcement gives no reason.
